items.title: Neoclouds Told To Choose: Nvidia Chips Or Chinese Customers
items.summary: Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) chip sellers are reportedly barring neoclouds from buying GPUs if Chinese firms rent any capacity, after a Commerce Department rule restricting remote access to AI chips took effect Nov. 19. Commerce Rule Targets Remote Access Loophole Chip sellers relayed the message to neoclouds after the rule was announced Nov. 16, CNBC reported on Thursday, citing sources. Neoclouds are specialized cloud providers that rent out computing power built on graphics processing units (GP

analysis.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department has enacted a rule barring cloud providers (neoclouds) from buying Nvidia GPUs if they rent more than 50% of capacity to Chinese firms, cutting off indirect sales to China.
analysis.catalyst: Commerce Department’s new export rule restricting remote access to Nvidia AI chips for Chinese renters
analysis.horizon: 4-6 weeks, until Nvidia’s quarterly guidance reflects the drop in GPU demand from neoclouds and any earnings beat/miss confirms the impact
analysis.explanation: The rule directly limits Nvidia's biggest growth engine – sales of its high‑end GPUs to cloud providers that serve Chinese AI workloads. Those neoclouds now must either drop Chinese customers or find alternative hardware, shrinking Nvidia's addressable market. Over the next month, we expect Nvidia's revenue guidance to be revised lower and the stock to price in this demand shock, especially given the neutral sentiment and already lofty valuation. While analysts are still raising price targets, the fundamental sales constraint outweighs short‑term optimism. A short position in NVDA captures the downside as the market digests reduced exposure to the Chinese AI segment.
rationale: Direct sales to Chinese AI users already blocked; this rule cuts the indirect channel via neoclouds
GPU demand is a key driver of Nvidia’s valuation – any reduction pressures the stock
Short horizon aligns with upcoming earnings where the impact will be quantified
analysis.risk: If the rule is softened or neoclouds find alternative ways to source Nvidia chips, the sales hit could be less severe, limiting downside.

analysis.horizon: 2-4 weeks, or until the company announces a clear timeline for resuming shipments in the region

Given the short‑term nature of the regulatory review, a short position in NVDA equity captures the expected price decline while we wait for a resolution or guidance from Nvidia on when shipments will resume.

analysis.horizon: 4-6 weeks, until Nike’s Q2 2025 earnings release (Dec 17) when the actual tariff impact will be reflected in EPS and margin guidance
analysis.explanation: Nike assumes only a 15% tariff headwind, but the proposed rates are significantly higher—20% to 35% for Vietnam and up to 20% for Indonesia and China. Because 95% of Nike’s shoe production is in those countries, the cost increase will directly erode its already thin gross margins, which fell to the low 40% range. The market has priced in a modest EPS rise for FY2028, but that forecast ignores the higher tariff scenario, creating a valuation gap. By shorting Nike now, we capture the downside risk if the tariffs are imposed at the higher end and Nike’s earnings miss expectations in its upcoming earnings report. The trade is focused on the equity rather than a broader consumer‑discretionary ETF because the catalyst is company‑specific and the margin impact is material.
rationale: Tariff rates likely to exceed Nike’s 15% assumption, hitting margins hard
Nike’s margin cushion is thin; little room to absorb cost shock
Earnings release in mid‑December will reveal the real impact, providing a clear exit point
analysis.risk: If the U.S. negotiates a lower tariff rate or Nike successfully passes costs to consumers, the earnings miss may not materialize and the stock could rebound.

items.title: Eli Lilly (LLY) Adds FDA Vision Warning To GLP 1 Drug Labels
items.summary: Eli Lilly (NYSE:LLY) and Novo Nordisk plan to add new FDA required warning labels to GLP-1 drugs tied to rare vision risks. The updated labels will reference non arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, or NAION, a serious but uncommon eye condition. The FDA label change affects GLP-1 treatments used in both obesity and diabetes care, tightening risk disclosure for prescribers and patients. The new NAION warning on GLP-1 labels arrives alongside broader themes our research has...

analysis.summary: The FDA is adding a new warning label for rare vision loss (NAION) to Eli Lilly's GLP‑1 obesity and diabetes drugs, including Mounjaro and Zepbound.
analysis.catalyst: FDA label amendment requiring NAION warning on GLP‑1 drugs
analysis.horizon: 3-6 months, until quarterly earnings show any slowdown in GLP‑1 sales or rising litigation reserves
analysis.explanation: The FDA’s label change flags a safety risk that could dampen physician prescribing and trigger lawsuits. GLP‑1 drugs are Lilly’s fastest‑growing revenue stream, so any hesitation from doctors or insurers could curb sales momentum. The neutral sentiment from the article masks the underlying negative impact on the risk profile, and analysts have already flagged litigation exposure as a headwind. Over the next few months we expect to see either a dip in prescription growth or an increase in legal reserves in Lilly’s quarterly filings, which would pressure the stock. A short position lets us profit if the market re‑prices this risk, while a long would be exposed to upside from continued strong demand despite the warning.
rationale: Regulatory warning raises safety and litigation concerns for Lilly's core GLP‑1 franchise
Potential slowdown in prescriptions or higher legal costs could hit earnings in the next quarter(s)
Short exposure captures downside if the market re‑prices the risk
analysis.risk: If GLP‑1 demand remains robust and litigation risk stays low, the warning may have minimal impact and the stock could rebound, eroding the short thesis.

items.title: Cathie Wood and 14 Other Big Funds Sold Deere Last Quarter, While 10 Bought. Who’s Right?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysOf 460 big funds that have filed 13Fs for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 15 sold Deere, Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest among them, and 10 bought.

analysis.summary: Big funds sold more Deere (DE) than bought in Q3, with sellers moving larger dollar amounts, while Deere trades at a high 31x forward earnings and gave a weak FY2027 guide.
analysis.catalyst: Quarterly 13F filings showing net large sales of Deere and the company's FY2027 earnings guidance below expectations
analysis.horizon: 4-6 weeks, until the next earnings release or a noticeable price correction toward its historical valuation multiple
analysis.explanation: Fund managers have collectively cut their Deere positions, dumping roughly $600 million versus only $57 million of new buying. That net selling pressure, combined with Deere's forward P/E of 31x—well above its five‑year average of 20x—suggests the stock is overvalued. The weak FY2027 earnings guidance further fuels the case for a price decline as analysts likely trim targets. Over the next month or so, we expect the market to re‑price Deere toward a more reasonable multiple, offering a short‑term upside for a short position. A short on DE captures the downside risk directly, whereas a broader market short or a CAT long would dilute the thesis.
rationale: Large net fund outflows signal bearish sentiment
Forward earnings multiple is stretched vs historical average
FY2027 guidance missed expectations, likely prompting price correction
analysis.risk: If Deere's agricultural sales rebound faster than expected or the broader market rallies, the stock could stay elevated, eroding short gains.
